blurb: Eight centuries on one footprint: the choir of 1163, towers and flying buttresses, the spire pulled down in 1792 and rebuilt in 1859, the fire of 2019 and the rebuilding.
Built in ten years, opened in 80, broken by the 1349 earthquake and quarried for centuries: the ruin you see today, placed on its real outline.
Two centuries of works on soft ground: the tower starts to sink in 1178, leans to 5.5° by 1990, and is pulled back to 3.97°.
18,038 iron parts on four legs, from the caissons dug under the Seine to the 300 m top, its first floor rebuilt in glass in 2015 and its illumination.
